bibl.title: Analysis of 100,000 human cancer genomes reveals the landscape of tumor mutational burden

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: tumour mutational burden as a biomarker - how it is counted, how little genome is enough to count it, and how it is distributed across cancer types
span.quote: An emerging biomarker for response to immunotherapy is the total number of mutations present in a tumor specimen. This is termed the mutation load or tumor mutational burden (TMB). It is hypothesized that highly mutated tumors are more likely to harbor neoantigens which make them targets of activated immune cells.

span.label: whether a 1.1 Mb targeted panel can stand in for whole exome sequencing when measuring mutational burden, and what the burden looks like across a hundred thousand clinical specimens
span.quote: We finally sought to determine the effects of sequencing different amounts of the genome and how that might affect our ability to accurately determine TMB. We sampled the number of mutations that we would expect to see at different TMB levels (100 mutations/Mb, 20 mutations/Mb, 10 mutations/Mb) and at different amounts of megabases sequenced, from 0.2 to 10 Mb, 1000 times for each TMB level and sequencing amount. For each sample, we then measured the percentage deviation from the whole exome TMB (Fig. 1c).

span.label: a validated targeted measurement of TMB, a downsampling analysis showing where it stops working, and the distribution of TMB across more than 100 tumour types
span.quote: We found that, as expected, the percentage deviation is lower for high underlying TMB, meaning that specimens with high TMB can be effectively identified by targeted sequencing of several hundred genes. In contrast, for intermediate levels of TMB, the percentage deviation starts to increase, especially with less than 0.5 Mb sequenced (Fig. 1c).

span.label: existence
span.quote: We found that microsatellite instability (MSI-High) generally occurred as a subset of high TMB (Fig. 3a). The vast majority of MSI-High samples also had high TMB (83%), and 97% had TMB ≥10 mutations/Mb. However, the converse was not true; only 16% of samples with high TMB were classified as MSI-High.

span.label: a clinical category - high mutational burden - whose membership depends on an assay's size, a list of exclusions, and a threshold stated once in a figure caption
span.quote: Specimens with TMB low and called as MSI-Stable are shown in light grey, specimens with high TMB (mutations/Mb >20) are shown in blue, and specimens called as MSI-High are shown in dark grey.

span.label: targeted comprehensive genomic profiling of 315 genes with germline filtering and no matched normal, validated against matched whole exome sequencing and against in-silico subsetting of TCGA exomes
span.term: targeted comprehensive genomic profiling of 315 genes with germline filtering and no matched normal, validated against matched whole exome sequencing and against in-silico subsetting of TCGA exomes
span.quote: For the WES samples, tumor and normal tissue were each sequenced in order to distinguish germline polymorphisms from somatic mutations. For the targeted CGP samples, no matched normal material was sequenced; rather, genomic variants were stringently filtered to eliminate germline polymorphisms (see “Methods” for details).

span.label: TMB is a rate estimated from a sample of the genome, so the fewer megabases read the noisier the estimate; the effect is worst where the underlying rate is low, because the expected count in the sampled region approaches zero
span.term: sampling variance rising as the panel shrinks
span.quote: We found that, as expected, the percentage deviation is lower for high underlying TMB, meaning that specimens with high TMB can be effectively identified by targeted sequencing of several hundred genes. In contrast, for intermediate levels of TMB, the percentage deviation starts to increase, especially with less than 0.5 Mb sequenced (Fig. 1c).

span.label: a synonymous change cannot itself create a neoantigen, but it is produced by the same mutational process that produced the nonsynonymous ones elsewhere, so counting it raises the sample size of the rate estimate without changing what the rate is about
span.term: synonymous mutations as a process signal
span.quote: Synonymous mutations are counted in order to reduce sampling noise. While synonymous mutations are not likely to be directly involved in creating immunogenicity, their presence is a signal of mutational processes that will also have resulted in nonsynonymous mutations and neoantigens elsewhere in the genome.

span.label: with no normal tissue sequenced, inherited variants must be removed by matching against reference databases - so the filter's accuracy is the databases' coverage of the patient's ancestry
span.term: germline filtering without a matched normal
span.quote: We found that filtering out germline alterations and rare variants was important to obtaining accurate measurements of TMB, and this will especially be important in patients from ethnic backgrounds not well represented in sequencing datasets.

span.label: the germline filter depends on reference databases, so it will be least accurate for patients from ethnic backgrounds not well represented in them - stated by the authors
span.quote: We found that filtering out germline alterations and rare variants was important to obtaining accurate measurements of TMB, and this will especially be important in patients from ethnic backgrounds not well represented in sequencing datasets.

span.label: the MSI cut points were set by manual unsupervised clustering against a reference that was itself partly APPROXIMATED by the same pipeline's homopolymer indel counts
span.quote: Ranges of the MSI score were assigned MSI-High (MSI-H), MSI-ambiguous, or microsatellite stable (MSS) by manual unsupervised clustering of specimens for which MSI status was previously assessed either via IHC if available or approximated by the number of homopolymer indel mutations detected by our standard pipeline.

span.label: the accuracy figure rests on 29 specimens with matched whole exome sequencing; the two 0.98 correlations are the assay against itself and an in-silico subsetting
span.quote: We found that the tumor mutation burden calculated by these two methods was highly correlated (R2 = 0.74; Fig. 1a). We also assessed the reproducibility of our method for calculating TMB using targeted CGP. For 60 samples for which CGP was performed more than once, we compared the TMB between replicates. We found that these values were highly correlated (R2 = 0.98), indicating that this method for measuring TMB has high precision (Fig. 1b).

span.label: known mismatch-repair and replication genes account for less than 10% of high-TMB cases, so the molecular basis of most of the phenomenon is unexplained
span.quote: We characterized the distribution and prevalence of coding mutations in known genes involved in mismatch repair and DNA replication. However, overall mutations in these genes accounted for less than 10% of cases with high TMB.

span.label: the PMS2 promoter mutations are not shown to be causal, and the TOP2A association rests on eight cases
span.quote: We have not definitively shown that these mutations are causal, and additional experiments will be needed to elucidate the function of these promoter mutations.

span.label: targeted profiling measures the burden but cannot identify the neoantigens the mechanism depends on, since those may occur in any gene
span.quote: While targeted CGP can be used to accurately assess TMB, it is not currently suited for identification of neoantigens, which might occur in any gene.

span.label: principal components analysis, carried from multivariate statistics to collapse 228 repeat-length measurements into a single MSI score that can be cut into categories
span.quote: To determine MSI status, 114 intronic homopolymer repeat loci with adequate coverage on the CGP panel were analyzed for length variability and compiled into an overall MSI score via principal components analysis. The 114 loci were selected from a total set of 1897 that have adequate coverage on the FMI FoundationOne bait set. Amongst the 1897 microsatellites, the 114 that maximized variability between samples were chosen.

span.label: resampling simulation, carried from survey methodology to ask how small a genomic panel may be before the rate it estimates stops being the rate
span.quote: We finally sought to determine the effects of sequencing different amounts of the genome and how that might affect our ability to accurately determine TMB. We sampled the number of mutations that we would expect to see at different TMB levels (100 mutations/Mb, 20 mutations/Mb, 10 mutations/Mb) and at different amounts of megabases sequenced, from 0.2 to 10 Mb, 1000 times for each TMB level and sequencing amount. For each sample, we then measured the percentage deviation from the whole exome TMB (Fig. 1c).

span.label: the same biopsy specimens measured by both the targeted panel and whole exome sequencing, so the panel is checked against a different measurement rather than against itself
span.note: eliminates: the targeted panel's own gene selection as the explanation of the burden it reports - the same biopsy measured by a method that selects no genes gives a correlated answer · outcome: partial
span.quote: We found that the tumor mutation burden calculated by these two methods was highly correlated (R2 = 0.74; Fig. 1a). We also assessed the reproducibility of our method for calculating TMB using targeted CGP. For 60 samples for which CGP was performed more than once, we compared the TMB between replicates. We found that these values were highly correlated (R2 = 0.98), indicating that this method for measuring TMB has high precision (Fig. 1b).

span.label: 60 replicate pairs run through the same assay, separating precision from accuracy
span.note: eliminates: assay noise as the explanation of the remaining disagreement with whole exome sequencing - the assay repeats itself at R2 0.98, so what is left is between methods and not within one · outcome: held
span.quote: We found that the tumor mutation burden calculated by these two methods was highly correlated (R2 = 0.74; Fig. 1a). We also assessed the reproducibility of our method for calculating TMB using targeted CGP. For 60 samples for which CGP was performed more than once, we compared the TMB between replicates. We found that these values were highly correlated (R2 = 0.98), indicating that this method for measuring TMB has high precision (Fig. 1b).

span.label: simulating the measurement at smaller panel sizes to find where sampling variance makes the estimate unusable, rather than asserting that 1.1 Mb is enough
span.note: eliminates: sampling variance as a hidden contributor at the panel size actually used - the simulation measures it rather than assuming 1.1 Mb is enough, and names where it stops being enough · outcome: partial
span.quote: We finally sought to determine the effects of sequencing different amounts of the genome and how that might affect our ability to accurately determine TMB. We sampled the number of mutations that we would expect to see at different TMB levels (100 mutations/Mb, 20 mutations/Mb, 10 mutations/Mb) and at different amounts of megabases sequenced, from 0.2 to 10 Mb, 1000 times for each TMB level and sequencing amount. For each sample, we then measured the percentage deviation from the whole exome TMB (Fig. 1c).

span.label: an independent check on 8,917 TCGA exomes, comparing total mutations against those in the 315 assay genes
span.note: eliminates: this laboratory's own cohort and pipeline as the source of the agreement - the same comparison on 8,917 independently generated exomes reproduces it · outcome: held
span.quote: We also analyzed whole-exome sequencing data from 35 studies, published as part of TCGA, examining a total of 8917 cancer specimens. We determined the number of mutations in total and compared that to the number of mutations in the 315 genes targeted by our assay. As expected, these results were also highly correlated (R2 = 0.98).

span.label: cohort filtering declared in advance - duplicates removed, coverage floor, and a minimum of 50 specimens before a cancer type is analysed at all
span.note: eliminates: duplicate specimens and under-covered samples as contributors to the reported distribution · outcome: held
span.quote: From an initial clinical cohort of 102,292 samples, duplicate assay results from the same patient were excluded, and samples with less that 300× median exon coverage were excluded to make an analysis set of 92,439 samples. For analyses by cancer type, they must contain a minimum of 50 unique specimens following sample level filtering.

span.label: checking whether more than the first principal component of the MSI score was needed
span.note: eliminates: further principal components as carriers of microsatellite signal the one-dimensional score discards - none of the others explains more than 4% of the variance · outcome: held
span.quote: There was no need to extend beyond the first principal component, as it explained ~50% of the total data variance, while none of the other principal components explained more than 4% each.

span.label: TMB
span.quote: TMB was defined as the number of somatic, coding, base substitution, and indel mutations per megabase of genome examined. All base substitutions and indels in the coding region of targeted genes, including synonymous alterations, are initially counted before filtering as described below.

span.quote: Assays that measure PD-1/PD-L1 protein expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC) are approved as complementary or companion diagnostics for some of these drugs; however, measurement of PD-1/PD-L1 expression is technically challenging, can be difficult to interpret, and is not always an accurate predictor of response to immunotherapy.
